messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2278 — elevated GPU VRAM fragmentation and intermittent OOMs in us-west-2 for inference-prod. Pager -> @alex.park. Severity: P2. Metrics: spike in allocation failures and increased tail latency. Link: https://grafana.company/r/inference-prod
alex.park: saw the alert, looking now. which fleet is noisy?
maria.gomez: looks like pool-gpu-a (nv4a) nodes 12, 19 showing repeated alloc failures. VRAM free dropping under 6GB then sudden OOMs.
alex.park: thanks. any customer impact?
maria.gomez: FYI SRE monitoring shows 2.1% of requests 5xx last 10m in us-west-2, a couple of e2e jobs timed out. not huge but visible.
jamal: can we reduce noisy paging by silencing the per-node low-vram alert for now and keep cluster-level alerts? avoid pager storms.
priya.singh: agree. silencing node-level until we mitigate. I'll apply 15m silence to alert rule `node_gpu_vram_low` on the alertmanager.
sre-lead: fine for short-term but capture why free VRAM fragments quickly. if it's allocator churn from a workload, we should fallback to a smaller batch size or quantized variant.
alex.park: checking which models are hitting those nodes. looks like batch-inference-worker-3 has long sequences + large batch windows. suggests fallback to quantized-small for older model version.
maria.gomez: rolling a temporary route rule in the router to steer new requests away from pool-gpu-a. small change: set capacity weight=0.2 for pool-gpu-a, route to pool-gpu-b.
jamal: if we need to take nodes out, command: ```kubectl drain node/gpu-a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
alex.park: don't drain until we confirm graceful handoff — we'll first reduce new connections and evict long-running jobs.
priya.singh: silence applied. alertmanager: `node_gpu_vram_low` suppressed for pool-gpu-a for 15m. :white_check_mark:
maria.gomez: started reroute in router-config. new requests draining off gpu-a nodes, existing pods still serving. latency should drop in 5-7m.
jamal: noticing ECC error counter on gpu-a-19 incrementing (small count) — not correlated with OOMs but worth watching. setting a short-term watch rule.
sre-lead: put an ECC alert threshold on a rate not an absolute: `increase(ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 2` to avoid noise from single retries.
alex.park: can we also introduce a VRAM free-derived alert that uses percentile across pool, e.g., `min_over_time(free_vram_bytes[5m]) < 4GB on count(nodes) >= 3`? right now individual node alerts firing for transient dips.
priya.singh: proposing new alert snippet (working draft):
```
- alert: Pool_Free_VRAM_Low
  expr: sum by (pool)(min_over_time(free_vram_bytes[5m])) < 4294967296
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Pool {{ $labels.pool }} free VRAM under 4GB for >5m"
```
maria.gomez: also let's add a moving-average panel to Grafana for `free_vram_bytes` and `alloc_failures` to reduce chasing spikes. I'll add panels: 1) pool 95p free_vram, 2) allocation_fail_rate per node, 3) ECC errors rate.
jamal: I ran a quick heap/allocator check on node gpu-a-12, found memory fragmentation (many small free regions). Restarting the local allocator service on that node freed ~3.5GB.
alex.park: can you put that restart command here?
jamal: ```systemctl restart gpu-allocator.service && journalctl -u gpu-allocator -n 200 --no-pager```
priya.singh: allocator restart on gpu-a-12 succeeded, node free VRAM jumped to ~9GB. no OOMs in last 2m.
maria.gomez: latency dropping, 5xx back to baseline. customer impact minimal but visible - we'll log a customer-impact note in the incident afterwards.
sre-lead: good mitigation. create post-incident action items: 1) add pool-level VRAM alert (owner: maria.gomez), 2) tune allocator GC to run more aggressively on long-lived nodes (owner: jamal), 3) add evict policy for long-running large-batch pods (owner: alex.park).
alex.park: I'll also add a temporary rollback for the batch-window config on batch-inference-worker-3 to smaller batch sizes for next 2 hours.
priya.singh: preparing handoff to next oncall. current shift ends in 40m. Jamal, can you take the 10:00-18:00 PST handoff and monitor pool-gpu-a for 2h? add Slack watch and update runbook if anything changes.
jamal: taking handoff. I will keep the suppression in place for the next 15m if needed and then we revert to normal alerting once the pool stabilizes.
maria.gomez: I've created a short-lived dashboard and linked it in the incident thread: https://grafana.company/d/incident-2278-gpu-vram. Saved annotations for allocator restart and silence.
oncall-bot: Incident 2278 acknowledged by alex.park, mitigation in progress. Current state: degraded -> stabilizing.
alex.park: moving this to monitoring/tune follow-up. I'll open an internal ticket with the action items and schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:
jamal: quick note for follow-up tuning: consider alert suppression window of 10m + require >2 nodes affected to page. reduces single-node flapping.
sre-lead: agreed. add to ticket and cc infra oncall.
priya.singh: handing over to Jamal. I'll be available on slack for 30m.#handoff
jamal: acknowledged. continuing watch.
oncall-bot: Incident 2278 status: monitoring; last update at 2278903860.
